title: Control Board Communication Error
shortDescription: The oven control board has lost internal communication.
fullDescription:
F0 on a Maytag oven indicates the electronic oven control (EOC) has failed a self-check or lost communication with its subsystems. Cooking functions are disabled.

A hard reset will clear transient faults; persistent F0 requires control board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat EOC connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear panel and reseat ribbon and power harnesses.

fixSteps.title: Replace EOC
fixSteps.instruction: Install new electronic oven control.

whenToCallPro: Recommended for 240V gas or electric ovens.

faq.q: Can I cook with F0?
faq.a: No — the oven is disabled until cleared.

title: EOC Internal Failure
fullDescription:
F1 indicates the oven control has failed a watchdog or ROM check. Maytag and Whirlpool-built ovens use this code to indicate generic EOC failure.

Replacement of the electronic oven control is usually required.

fixSteps.title: Reset power
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle breaker for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace EOC
fixSteps.instruction: Install new electronic oven control.

whenToCallPro: Recommended for board-level work.

faq.q: Is a surge protector helpful?
faq.a: Yes — especially for ovens on storm-prone circuits.

title: Oven Over-Temperature
shortDescription: Oven cavity temperature exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the oven cavity temperature has risen above the safe threshold (around 650F in bake, 950F in clean). The control cuts power to protect components.

Causes include a welded relay, a failing temperature sensor, or a stuck door lock during self-clean.

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off breaker immediately.

fixSteps.title: Test temperature sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify RTD reads 1080 ohms at room temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace EOC or sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the failed part.

whenToCallPro: Strongly recommended — over-temp is a safety fault.

faq.q: Can I skip self-clean?
faq.a: Yes — manual cleaning avoids self-clean related F2 faults.

title: Open Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor (RTD) circuit is open.
fullDescription:
F3 means the control reads an open circuit where the RTD temperature sensor should be. Either the sensor has failed, the harness is broken, or the EOC is defective.

A quick continuity test identifies the issue.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check RTD resistance — should be ~1080 ohms at 70F.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new RTD sensor.

whenToCallPro: If harness routing requires oven removal.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F3 temperature sensor fix

faq.q: Where is the sensor?
faq.a: Upper rear of oven cavity; held by two screws.

title: Shorted Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: The RTD temperature sensor is shorted.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates a shorted RTD sensor circuit — the opposite of F3. The control reads extremely low resistance as if the probe itself has shorted or the wiring is pinched.

Replace the RTD sensor and inspect for damaged wiring.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; very low values indicate short.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new RTD sensor.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F4 shorted sensor fix

faq.q: Difference from F3?
faq.a: F3 is open circuit; F4 is shorted.

title: Door Latch Failure
shortDescription: The self-clean door latch mechanism has failed.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates the self-clean door lock failed to reach or release its locked position within the allowed time. A failed door lock motor or stuck linkage is typical.

Self-clean cycles are suspended until resolved.

fixSteps.title: Cool oven
fixSteps.instruction: Allow oven to fully cool; lock may release.

fixSteps.title: Replace lock assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install new door lock motor and switches.

whenToCallPro: If door remains locked and inaccessible.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F5 door latch fix

faq.q: Can I open the door?
faq.a: Wait for full cool-down; forcing can damage the mechanism.

title: Line Frequency Error
fullDescription:
F6 indicates the oven sensed AC line frequency outside of 50/60Hz tolerances. This can happen on generators or with a failing EOC.

Verify household voltage and consider EOC replacement if voltage is normal.

fixSteps.title: Verify power source
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm unit is on utility (not generator).

fixSteps.title: Replace EOC
fixSteps.instruction: Install new electronic oven control.

whenToCallPro: If voltage issues persist, call an electrician.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F6 frequency error fix

faq.q: Is a UPS needed?
faq.a: A line conditioner helps on unstable circuits.

title: Stuck Function Key
shortDescription: A function key on the control is stuck.
fullDescription:
F7 indicates a control key has been detected as pressed continuously for more than a minute. Typical causes are a failed membrane switch, a bulging overlay, or EOC issues.

Replace the touch membrane or EOC.

fixSteps.title: Inspect overlay
fixSteps.instruction: Check for physical damage to keypad.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Install new touchpad/overlay assembly.

whenToCallPro: If EOC replacement is also required.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F7 stuck key fix

faq.q: Can I silence the beep?
faq.a: Cut breaker power to stop it while you work.

title: Analog Board or Display Failure
shortDescription: Communication with the display board failed.
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the EOC cannot communicate with the user interface/display board. Usually the display board or ribbon connector has failed.

Replace the display board or ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Reconnect display ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new display/UI module.

whenToCallPro: For back-of-unit wiring work.

faq.q: Do I need to replace EOC too?
faq.a: Usually no — the UI board is separate.

title: Door Latch Error (Non-Clean)
shortDescription: Door latch switch reports inconsistent state.
fullDescription:
F9 indicates the door latch switch reports an impossible state combination — locked and unlocked simultaneously, or no signal at all.

This differs from F5 in that it is not tied to self-clean; it can interrupt normal bake cycles.

fixSteps.title: Inspect latch
fixSteps.instruction: Check latch for free movement.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install new door lock/latch.

whenToCallPro: If disassembly of oven cavity is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F9 latch error fix

faq.q: Can I bake with F9?
faq.a: No — the control blocks heating until cleared.

title: Runaway Temperature Condition
shortDescription: Oven is heating without being commanded.
fullDescription:
F10 signals that the oven is heating even though no command has been issued — typically a welded element relay on the EOC.

This is a safety-critical fault: shut off power at the breaker until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Shut off breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Immediately cut power.

fixSteps.title: Replace EOC
fixSteps.instruction: Install new oven control board.

whenToCallPro: Strongly recommended due to fire risk.

faq.q: Is it dangerous?
faq.a: Yes — keep breaker off until repaired.

title: Shorted Keypad
shortDescription: The keypad has a shorted button.
fullDescription:
F11 indicates the EOC detects a shorted touchpad — different from a simple stuck key. The membrane circuit has likely failed internally.

Replacement of the touchpad/overlay is typically required.

fixSteps.title: Let dry
fixSteps.instruction: If recent cleaning spill, let the oven sit powered off overnight.

fixSteps.title: Replace touchpad
fixSteps.instruction: Install new overlay/touchpad assembly.

whenToCallPro: If EOC also needs swapping.
videoSearchQuery: Maytag oven F11 shorted keypad fix

faq.q: Difference from F7?
faq.a: F7 is a stuck key; F11 is an internal short.

title: Oven EOC Watchdog Failure
shortDescription: Electronic oven control internal watchdog tripped.
fullDescription: F1-E1 indicates the EOC's internal watchdog detected a firmware fault. EOC replacement is usually required.
symptoms: Cycle may abort or fail to start

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the oven
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker for 2 minutes, then restore power. Some transient faults clear with a reset.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring and connections
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the oven out and inspect the harness related to the EOC replacement. Look for chafe, burn marks, or loose connectors.

fixSteps.title: Test the suspect component
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to test the EOC replacement and confirm whether it is in spec. Reference the service manual for expected values.

fixSteps.title: Replace the failed component
fixSteps.instruction: If the EOC replacement tests bad, replace it with the manufacturer-specified part. Reassemble in reverse order and verify operation.

whenToCallPro: If component replacement does not resolve, the control board may need professional diagnosis and replacement.

faq.q: Can I keep using the oven with this error?
faq.a: It is best to resolve before continued use to avoid further damage or safety risk.

faq.q: What does professional repair cost?
faq.a: Typically $180-$650 depending on the failed component and labor rates.

faq.q: Will a power cycle fix this permanently?
faq.a: Sometimes, but a recurring code points to a real hardware or wiring fault that needs repair.
